subject: Exogenous variable effect coded (-1 / 1) possible in lavaan?

messages.author: 772e580edc5b4e79
messages.subject: Exogenous variable effect coded (-1 / 1) possible in lavaan?
parts:
Hi all,

a reviewer has asked me whether I can account for measurement error in my DV for a linear mixed regressions (clusters of repeated measures = ID).

My go to solution would be to model my DV as latent construct (4 Items) and use the categorical (experimental conditions/groups) IVs as predictors. Effectively replicating a regression with a better way to measure the DV.
In the initial model, I have opted for effect coding (-1/1) for my IVs.

Now I am wondering, will Lavaan create wrong estimates if I used my experimental conditions as IV that are coded as -1 / 1?

This is what the model looks like

model<-
'DV=~x1+x2+x3+x4

DV~y1+y2+y1:y2+age+gender'

y1: Group a =-1; Group b = +1
y2: Group c =-1; Group d = +1
age: continuous
gender: dummy coded 0/1
clusters of repeated measures = ID
Grouping dataset: Country

sem(model, data = df, estimator="MLR", group = "Country", cluster="ID")


I could not find any explanation about this. Intuitively, I would say it should not matter. However, running the same model with dummy coded variables for y1 and y2 gives me different estimates.
Any help would be appreciated.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Exogenous variable effect coded (-1 / 1) possible in lavaan?
parts: Now I am wondering, will Lavaan create wrong estimates if I used my experimental conditions as IV that are coded as -1 / 1?

Define "wrong".  If you are comparing your results to a regression model that controls for Country using dummy/effects codes, the estimates will differ from a multigroup SEM that estimates an intercept for each Country.  The same could be done in a regression model that excludes the (fixed) intercept, so that each Country's dummy code is included (i.e., no reference group).  But then each other predictor's effect would need to be moderated by Country as well, unless you are equating them across groups in the SEM.
running the same model with dummy coded variables for y1 and y2 gives me different estimates

Because a 1-unit difference does not mean the same thing for a dummy code (treatment vs. control) as for an effect code (treatment vs. average of treatment/control groups).  If you want the same 1-unit effect, you could use effect codes -0.5 and +0.5.
